h: פָּרָשַׁת שְׁקָלִים, מַאֲמָר א׳ Parshas Shekalim — Maamar Aleph

p: One must examine closely why they instituted
קְרִיאַת הַפָּרָשָׁה בַּשַּׁבָּת שֶׁלִּפְנֵי רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ
the reading of the parshah on the Shabbos before Rosh Chodesh
and not on Rosh Chodesh Adar itself,
for that is when they announce concerning the shekalim,
and the reading of the parshah takes the place of the proclamation to announce it,
וְהָיָה לָהֶם לְתַקֵּן זֶה בְּרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ.
so they should have instituted it on Rosh Chodesh.
And even without this, a reason is needed
for the institution of the reading itself:
for in the time of the Beis HaMikdash, when they would announce
what need was there to read the parshah as well
And now that they do not announce,
what need is there for reading the parshah,
since we have no Beis HaMikdash
and there is no need to give the shekalim at all?
And in Tanchuma, Ki Sisa, at the end of siman 3:
"and the parshiyos that are read..." etc.,
"they mention him in each and every parshah,
and in Parshas Shekalim Moshe said..." etc.,
"once I die I will not be remembered.
אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא כְּשֵׁם וְכוּלֵּי
The Holy One, blessed is He, said to him: Just as..." etc.,
כָּךְ בְּכָל שָׁנָה שֶׁקּוֹרִין אוֹתָהּ לְפָנַי
"so every year that they read it before Me,
it is as if you are standing at that time
and lifting up their heads." End of quote.
הִנֵּה דִּקְרִיאַת פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ בְּכָל שָׁנָה
We see that reading this parshah every year
is in order to lift up
and raise the head of Bnei Yisrael.
in what way is the head lifted by this?
And there, the raising of the head
דְּעַל זֶה אָמַר כִּי תִשָּׂא וְגוֹמֵר
for about this it says, "When you lift up..." etc.,
"according to their numbering..." etc., "when you count..." etc.
On the simple level it appears
that counting indicates the importance of the thing,
and as they said for this reason,
that anything sold by count is not nullified,
and the Chachamim say only six items:
and are customarily sold by count.
denotes being elevated above the rest,
as in "the heads of the tribes,"
and we find both together in Yechezkel (38:2)
It is like "He who is exalted as head above all,"
for the one who is exalted is the head and the first,
like the head of a person
And Hashem, may He be blessed, commanded
to lift up the head of all of Yisrael, every one of them.
is distinguished and exalted in some matter
in which there is none like him in all of Yisrael
as is known that the root of the souls of Yisrael
the six hundred thousand of the generation of the wilderness
And therefore they said in the Midrash
that had even one of them been missing,
the Torah would not have been given.
For a single letter would have been missing
or part of a letter, which disqualifies,
and a Sefer Torah is invalid when a letter is missing,
and even the tip of a yud is indispensable;
and for this reason they were counted.
And they said in the Zohar (III 117b)
that they are "the hosts of the Torah,"
for the number of these souls
And the souls in each generation
who are among the descendants of the generation of the wilderness
stem from the new insights of Torah she'b'al peh
which flows and issues forth from the Written Torah,
like the light of the moon, which receives from the sun
and the total number is six hundred thousand,
the number of the generation of the wilderness,
who are the root of the souls of all the generations,
as they said in Koheles Rabbah 1
that no generation has fewer than six hundred thousand.
that upon seeing multitudes of Yisrael one says,
"Blessed is He Who knows the secrets,"
for their minds are not like one another,
and a multitude is no less than six hundred thousand
for the mind of each one individually
accords with his root in the Torah.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ (תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּקּוּן יג כט, א)
And therefore they said (Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 13, 29a):
since they are all his descendants
and a portion of his soul,
and the totality of their souls is included in him.
And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
who is in the secret of Daas, as is known —
דְּעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר דּוֹר דֵּעָה
which is why the generation of the wilderness is called "the generation of knowledge,"
עַל פָּסוּק [מְלָכִים א ה, יא] וְדַרְדַּע
for he encompasses all the souls
which is the inner dimension of the soul.
As is known, regarding the ten sefiros,
from the aspect of their outer dimension,
Daas is not counted among them,
but only from the aspect of the inner dimension,
for it is what is called Ayin, Nothingness,
and the crown of the head where tefillin are placed,
and Chochmah, which is the beginning of revelation,
meaning what is grasped by man,
Daas fills the place of Kesser.
For Rashi in Parshas Ki Sisa
which is a perception that is above
and beyond the bounds of its grasp.
וְעַל כֵּן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And therefore Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
הוּא הַפְּנִימִיּוּת שֶׁל כָּל נַפְשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
is the inner dimension of all the souls of Yisrael,
that stems from the root and source of the soul
in the letters of the Torah;
and he is the Daas within the souls of all Yisrael
And therefore it is stated in the Gemara
said in astonishment: Where is your knowledge?
And in every generation there is also
of the heads of the thousands of Yisrael,
which encompass many thousands of souls.
And there are leaders of the generation
like Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
and they have a root from Moshe;
and as the Arizal, of blessed memory, wrote
on the expression "Moshe, are you speaking well?"
that the great one of the generation is called so
because he is a spark of Moshe Rabbeinu,
which is reincarnated in every generation.
Rav Chanina the son of Rav Ika
made a blessing upon Rav Pappa
and Rav Huna the son of Rav Yehoshua:
and he said to them: "Since I saw you,
I considered you, for me, like six hundred thousand";
וַאֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ חֲכִימַת כּוּלֵּי הַאי וְכוּלֵּי
and they said to him, "Are you that wise?" and so on;
And they considered this great wisdom,
that he perceived, through his seeing them
in the manner of what is said in the Zohar, Yisro,
on the verse "And you shall discern",
that they were equivalent to six hundred thousand,
the souls of the whole generation,
and were composed of six hundred thousand minds.
And as for what he said, "to me,"
one can say that this means
that he grasped this by seeing them,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּעֵירוּבִין י״ג ב׳
in the manner of what is said in Eruvin 13b:
"The reason I am sharper than my colleagues
is that I saw Rabbi Meir..." and so on;
the heart of each and every one
and the wisdom of each and every one;
he grasped the heart and wisdom of six hundred thousand.
וּמְבָרְכִין עַל זֶה לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
And for this one blesses the Holy One, blessed is He,
שֶׁבְּכָל אֶחָד מֵהֶם יֵשׁ רָז וְסוֹד
for within each one of them there is a mystery and secret
of his own, which is the root of his soul.
that within each one there is
some root of words of Torah;
and about this they said, "Who is wise?
One who learns from every person."
since only in the soul of Yisrael
יֵשׁ בְּכָל אֶחָד אֵיזֶה דְּבַר חָכְמָה
is there in each one some matter of wisdom
unique to him, from which his soul is rooted.
וְעַל כֵּן רַק עַל אוּכְלְסֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
Therefore only upon multitudes of Yisrael
does one bless "He Who knows the secrets,"
for His wisdom, may He be blessed, encompasses
And the wisdom of all the sages of Yisrael
is a portion of His wisdom, may He be blessed,
as they instituted in the blessing
said over the sages of Yisrael:
"Who has apportioned of His wisdom to those who fear Him";
and these are the sages of Yisrael,
in whom there is revealed wisdom.
And every other individual of Yisrael
of His wisdom, may He be blessed,
hidden in the root of his soul,
which he himself does not know,
and it is the root of his vitality,
"And wisdom gives life to those who possess it."
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יֵשׁ לְכָל אֶחָד
And through this, each one has
an elevation of the head above all of Yisrael,
by virtue of the portion of G-d from above
that is in the root of his soul,
in which there is a mystery and secret
And this is what they said there, in the chapter HaRo'eh:
that their minds are not alike
and their faces do not resemble one another;
for the difference in a person's form
comes from the difference in the mind within each one,
for the face, the face of a man,
is in the image of G-d,
and this is by virtue of the soul, a portion of G-d;
and "a man's wisdom lights up his face."
And each one, according to the point
of wisdom and knowledge within him,
which does not resemble his fellow's,
כֵּן אוֹר הַפָּנִים שֶׁלּוֹ אֵין דּוֹמֶה.
so too the light of his face is not alike.
And in Sanhedrin (38a) it is stated
a person differs from his fellow:
in voice, in appearance, and in mind.
And the voice too is drawn
for this is the essence of the vitality of the human form,
are differentiated by virtue of the Sitra Achra
and the kelipos, from which their souls are rooted;
and therefore it says about them,
for when they are gathered together —
is bad for them and bad for the world"
and "his hidden things are sought out,"
so that they are shamed in their root.
And their evil source is their mother
for each one has a particular root of evil,
and in their gathering it becomes an all-inclusive evil.
And the opposite is so with the gathering of the righteous,
and "the righteous one is the foundation of the world."
"Each and every one is obligated to say,
'For my sake the world was created,'"
for in truth, for the sake of each one
and as they said in Berachos (6b)
"for this is the whole of man":
And the entire world was created
only for the sake of this one,
to be a companion to this one;
and this applies to every individual,
כִּי כָּל אֶחָד הוּא מְדוּגָּל וּמְנוּשָּׂא
for each one is distinguished and exalted
in a unique matter of his own,
שֶׁעֲבוּר זֶה כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ בִּשְׁבִילוֹ
on account of which the whole world exists for his sake,
and they need him for this.
שֶׁאֵין לְךָ אָדָם שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שָׁעָה
"There is no person who does not have his hour,"
for everything in the world is
as they said in Sefer Yetzirah
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁבְּנֵי אָדָם חֲלוּקִים זֶה מִזֶּה
and just as people differ from one another,
each hour differs from the next,
all according to the division of the souls
that the hour stands for him,
meaning that at that time he was
the exalted one and the head,
for his vitality and the root of his soul
is the one elevated at that hour
And regarding the wicked it is called
in Berachos (7b) and in several places,
in the manner of "He Who sits in heaven laughs,
וְכֵן לְכָל אֶחָד יֵשׁ אֵיזוֹ שָׁעָה
and likewise each one has some hour
when Hashem, may He be blessed, desires
And then that hour stands for him,
for him to be the exalted one.

paragraphs.text: Mishnah Shekalim 1:1 — “On the first of Adar they make announcements concerning the shekalim and concerning mixed plantings.” The announcement initiates the collection of the annual half-shekel. Rav Tzadok asks why the public Torah reading precedes this announcement rather than coinciding with it.

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 3 — “Moshe taught Torah to Israel, guided them in the commandments, and gave them the Torah readings read each Shabbos, each month, and each festival; they mention him in every reading. Concerning the section of shekalim, Moshe said before the Holy One, blessed be He: 'Master of the world, after I die I will no longer be remembered.' The Holy One, blessed be He, told him: 'By your life, just as you now stand and give them the section of shekalim and lift up their heads, so each and every year when they read it before Me, it is as though you were standing there at that moment and lifting up their heads.'”

paragraphs.text: Beitzah 3b — “Rabbi Meir would say: That which is customarily counted renders the mixture prohibited. The Sages say: Only six things render it prohibited; Rabbi Akiva says: Seven. These are Perech nuts, Badan pomegranates, sealed casks, beet shoots, cabbage stalks, and the Greek gourd. Rabbi Akiva adds the loaves of a householder.” The discussion distinguishes competing definitions of the important items that resist nullification. Rav Tzadok uses their being counted as an illustration of recognized importance; the cited opinions do not all establish the same legal category.

paragraphs.text: Numbers 30:2; 13:3; 1:4 — “Moshe spoke to the heads of the tribes of the children of Israel, saying: This is the matter Hashem commanded. ... Moshe sent them from the wilderness of Paran at Hashem’s command; they were all men of standing, heads of the children of Israel. ... With you there shall be one man from each tribe, each a head of his ancestral house.” These three passages use head for a position of precedence or leadership. They establish the linguistic basis of Rav Tzadok’s distinction between being counted and being raised above others.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 117b, Bamidbar — “Once the Torah and the Mishkan had been established, the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to count the hosts of the Torah: how many were the hosts of the Torah, and how many were the hosts of the Mishkan. Come and see: anything that needs to be established in its place is not established until it is mentioned aloud and appointed over. Here too, the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to count the hosts of the Torah and the hosts of the Mishkan. They were all as one and were not separated from one another, all patterned after what is above; for Torah and Mishkan are not separated from one another, and they go together.” The retrieved source marks this passage as Vilna folio 117b. Rav Tzadok interprets Israel’s census through the Zohar’s designation of Israel as the hosts of the Torah.

paragraphs.text: Koheles Rabbah, on Ecclesiastes 1:4 — “A generation goes and a generation comes. Rabbi Yudan said in the name of Rabbi Levi: There is no day on which six hundred thousand are not born and six hundred thousand do not die. What is the reason? A generation goes and a generation comes. ... How do we know that a generation is six hundred thousand? For it is said: If any man among these people, this evil generation, shall see—and that generation numbered six hundred thousand.” In the retrieved verse-based numbering this is the exposition of Ecclesiastes 1:4. The Midrash speaks of the number of a generation; Rav Tzadok’s formulation, no generation has fewer, condenses its teaching for his discussion of the collective soul-roots.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 58a — “The Sages taught: One who sees the multitudes of Israel says, 'Blessed is the Knower of secrets,' for their minds are unlike one another and their faces are unlike one another. It was taught: A multitude numbers no fewer than six hundred thousand.” The blessing acknowledges God's knowledge of the inward differences concealed within an outwardly gathered multitude. Rav Tzadok identifies those differences with the distinct Torah-root of each soul.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 13, 29a — “When the sukkah was completed with its thigh, it was said of Yaakov: Yaakov came complete. Yaakov is indeed the image of the middle pillar from its outer aspect. Was Moshe not there too? Rather, he was from the inner aspect: this one from the body, and that one from the soul.” The source itself distinguishes outer and inner as body and soul. Rav Tzadok applies that distinction to Yaakov’s encompassing Israel through descent and Moshe’s encompassing their inward daas.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Tanya, Likkutei Amarim 42 — “Every soul of the house of Israel contains something of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him. ... Moshe Rabbeinu encompasses them all and is called the faithful shepherd, meaning that he draws daas into the community of Israel, so that each person may know Hashem according to the apprehension and higher root of his soul and its nurture from the root of Moshe Rabbeinu’s soul. paragraphs.text: Shaar HaGilgulim, Introduction 36, passage on Hillel — “Hillel was one spark among the six hundred thousand sparks of the root of Moshe Rabbeinu’s soul, which reincarnates in every generation. Therefore both were humble, and both lived one hundred and twenty years.” This passage supplies an explicit example in the writings of Rabbi Chaim Vital of a later sage as a spark from Moshe’s soul-root. It establishes the underlying teaching. The Arizal's explanation of the expression itself is transmitted by the Chida, Midbar Kedmus, Ma'areches Mem, os 7: “‘Moshe, you have spoken well’ is said in several places in the Talmud, and our master the Arizal explained that every outstanding Torah scholar in his generation has in him a spark of Moshe Rabbeinu.”

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 58b — “Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua were traveling and met Rav Chanina son of Rav Ika. They told him: 'On seeing you we recited two blessings: Who has apportioned of His wisdom to those who fear Him, and Who has kept us alive.' He replied: 'I too, when I saw you, regarded you as equivalent to six hundred thousand of the house of Israel and recited three blessings over you: those two, and the Knower of secrets.' They said to him: 'Are you so very wise!' They set their eyes upon him, and he died.” The account's severe ending belongs to the source and should not be omitted from its context. Rav Tzadok focuses on Rav Chanina's extraordinary recognition of the collective spiritual scope of these two sages.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 70a, Yitro, Raza deRazin — “We have learned that Moshe found this difficult until the Shechinah came and taught him. She perceived and selected all those men who were recognizable through their countenance, and there Moshe learned this wisdom and entered into it. This is what is written: And you shall perceive from among all the people—the One of whom it is written: You are He, and Your years will not end; You give life to them all; You, Hashem, are a shield for me. And you shall perceive and look into this: you, and no other, to know and contemplate the six hundred thousand.” This is the opening of Raza deRazin, whose digital source explicitly marks folio 70a. It concerns discernment of inward character through outward appearance and specifically joins that discernment with Moshe and the six hundred thousand.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 88a — “Rabbi Simai expounded: When Israel placed 'We will do' before 'We will hear,' six hundred thousand ministering angels came, and tied two crowns to each individual of Israel, one corresponding to 'We will do' and one to 'We will hear.' Rabbi Elazar said: When Israel placed 'We will do' before 'We will hear,' a heavenly voice went forth: 'Who revealed to My children this secret used by the ministering angels?' For it is written: 'Bless Hashem, His angels, mighty in strength, who perform His word, to hear the voice of His word'—first performing, and afterward hearing.” This is the source both for the two crowns and for the angelic precedence of doing over hearing. Its account of Moshe receiving the lost crowns and their eventual restoration also underlies the ensuing discussion.

paragraphs.text: Vayikra Rabbah 1:1 — “Rabbi Tanchum bar Chanilai opened: 'Bless Hashem, His angels, mighty in strength, who perform His word.' Of whom does Scripture speak? If it speaks of those above, has it not already said: 'Bless Hashem, all His hosts'? It therefore speaks of those below. Concerning those above, who can fulfill the assignments of the Holy One, blessed be He, it says 'all His hosts.' But concerning those below, who cannot fulfill His assignments, it says 'His angels,' and not 'all His angels.'” The Midrash subsequently interprets the mighty ones as those who observe Shemittah, and also as Israel at Sinai who put doing before hearing. Rav Tzadok develops its opening distinction in relation to human transmitters of Torah.

paragraphs.text: Chagigah 15b — “How could Rabbi Meir learn Torah from Acher? Rabbi Yochanan said: If the teacher resembles an angel of Hashem of Hosts, Torah should be sought from his mouth; otherwise, Torah should not be sought from his mouth. ‘There is no difficulty: one case concerns a mature person, the other an immature one.’ ... Rava expounded: Why are Torah scholars compared to a nut? Just as a nut, although soiled with mud and filth, has contents that do not become repulsive, so a Torah scholar, although he has gone astray, does not thereby render his Torah repulsive. ... Rabbah bar Sheila said to Eliyahu: 'Rabbi Meir found a pomegranate; he ate its inside and discarded its rind.'” The nut and the pomegranate are two distinct images in the same discussion. The former preserves the value of the Torah within; the latter describes Rabbi Meir’s exceptional ability to separate it from the teacher’s corrupt influence. The distinction concerning the learner prevents the passage from becoming an unrestricted license.

Ha lan veha lehu — “The Sages taught: If one must learn Torah and marry, he should learn Torah and then marry; if he cannot remain without a wife, he should marry and then learn. Rather, the righteous sit with their crowns on their heads and delight in the radiance of the Divine Presence, as it is said: 'They beheld God, and ate and drank.'” Rav Tzadok identifies these crowns with those bestowed at Sinai and destined to be restored; that identification joins this statement with the Shabbos 88a passage quoted earlier.

paragraphs.text: Arachin 11a — “Rav Masna said: From here—'Because you did not serve Hashem your God with joy and with goodness of heart.' What service is performed with joy and goodness of heart? You must say: This is song. But perhaps it means words of Torah, as it is written: 'Hashem's precepts are upright, gladdening the heart'! They are called gladdening the heart, but are not called good.” The sugya's question explicitly establishes Torah's power to gladden the heart, using Psalms 19:9. Its answer distinguishes that description from the combined wording by which it identifies the Levitical song.

paragraphs.text: Pri Etz Chaim, Shaar HaShabbos 8 — “When Moshe ascended the mountain to receive the Torah, they gave him a thousand portions of light. When Israel made the Calf, these were lost to him because of Israel's sin, leaving him one portion alone. Moshe himself had not sinned; the loss came on account of Israel. The Holy One, blessed be He, therefore made up his loss from Israel's crowns and lights, the ornaments stripped from them at Chorev. Every Friday night Moshe again receives the thousand portions that he lost, receiving them as the added gift of Shabbos. He then returns Israel's crowns to them, and from these crowns Israel inherits the added gift of Shabbos. ... He rejoices in his own portion and returns their portion to them. Since You called him a faithful servant, he returns those crowns of Israel held in his trust to their owners.” Pri Etz Chaim distinguishes Moshe's own original light from Israel's crowns held by him in trust. His own portion is restored on Shabbos, permitting him to return theirs. Rav Tzadok identifies the resulting addition for Israel with the additional soul.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 57b — “Five things are one-sixtieth of something else: fire, honey, Shabbos, sleep, and a dream. Fire is one-sixtieth of Gehinnom; honey, one-sixtieth of the manna; Shabbos, one-sixtieth of the World to Come; sleep, one-sixtieth of death; and a dream, one-sixtieth of prophecy.” The Gemara describes Shabbos as a present foretaste of the World to Come. Rav Tzadok combines this with the Zohar's account of the additional soul.

p: אָמַר לוֹ רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם וְכוּלֵּי
He said to Him, "Master of the World..." etc.,
"just as You lifted up my head"
see there at length, before this
The Holy One, blessed is He, said to him,
And one can explain what He told him,
means that he should return the crowns to them;
to return them entirely as they were,
since they had already sinned and they were taken;
and on Shabbos, what he returns
and this is not enough for lifting the head;
and therefore he said to Him,
וְהִסְכִּים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל יָדוֹ
and the Holy One, blessed is He, agreed with him
in what He said, "When you lift up..." etc.,
for in Tanchuma, Parshas Ki Sisa,
And this is because what is said,
"and on the day that I remember, I will visit..." etc.,
means that when He comes to count
which is the elevation of their heads,
which is the return of the crowns,
then the accusation is aroused again
on account of which they had been removed,
and a plague too could come,
For the removal of the crowns
rather, it is in the manner of what they said
for we learned: A dark house —
in the name of the Arizal, of blessed memory,
that when a person is raised
then a minor sin is aroused,
which, while he was in Gan Eden
was not considered a sin at all
or which he had already rectified,
so as to become like merits,
and in this manner with the sin of the Calf,
for they had already repented, and it was forgiven,
and He was appeased on Yom HaKippurim,
וְעִם כָּל זֶה לֹא הָיָה לְגַמְרֵי
and nevertheless it was not complete,
for then they would have returned
to what was at the giving of the Torah,
with the removal of the yetzer
and they judge him for that sin,
וְצָרִיךְ לְקַבֵּל עוֹנֶשׁ עַל זֶה מֵחָדָשׁ
and he must receive punishment for it anew,
even though he already received punishments beforehand
and was purified to be in Gan Eden.
And so too, "on the day that I remember..." etc.;
for this He commanded to give then
the shekalim as an atonement for the soul,
so that through this it will not be able
and bring a plague, Heaven forbid.
אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
Moshe said before the Holy One, blessed is He,
"Through what will the horn of Yisrael be raised?"
He said to him, "Through 'When you lift up.'"
"take from them an atonement for tzedakah."
But in truth, the verse speaks
of shekalim for the Mishkan and Mikdash,
and tzedakah for the poor is not mentioned at all,
But the whole discussion in the Gemara there,
and afterward too it cites verses:
"He has scattered, he has given to the needy..." etc.,
"his horn shall be exalted with honor";
when there is no Beis HaMikdash,
is effective as an atonement for the soul,
like the shekalim of the Beis HaMikdash.
only an atonement for the soul
when He lifts up their heads, so that it will cause no harm,
there is the lifting of the head —
one must say, according to what was explained,
that the raising of the horn
is through the return of the crowns,
and the atonement of the shekalim
is to atone for the Calf,
on account of which they were removed.
when this is atoned for through the atonement,
through this they will automatically return,
and they will come to the raising of the horn.

paragraphs.text: Pesikta Rabbasi 10, the passage cited as section 6 — “When Moshe descended to meet Israel, they saw him as something exalted and praiseworthy. At that moment Israel was distressed. They said: 'We are brought low because we did that deed. Although the Holy One, blessed be He, has accepted us and forgiven our sins, and you, Moshe, were with us, Moshe's rays are raised while our horns remain low.' Moshe immediately came before the Holy One, blessed be He, and said: 'Master of the world, when You brought them low, I too was brought low with them. Now that You have raised my head, raise their heads as well.' The Holy One, blessed be He, told him: 'Go, raise their heads.' Rabbi Yonasan of Beis Guvrin said: He replied, 'No, my Master! Just as You raised mine, so You should lift the heads of Your children.' The Holy One, blessed be He, told him: 'Just as I raised your head, so I too will raise the heads of My children: When you lift up the head of the children of Israel.'” The Midrash links Moshe's rays of glory and Israel's renewed elevation after the Golden Calf. Rav Tzadok interprets the exchange through the restoration of the crowns. The digital edition presents this passage within chapter 10 without the manuscript's internal section numbering.

Here the half-shekel becomes the means of atonement following the Calf.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 92a — “Rabbi Elazar said: Always remain obscure and endure. Rabbi Zeira said: We too have learned the same principle: One does not open windows in a dark house in order to inspect its plague-mark. Learn it from this.” Here kavel means remaining in obscurity, as the example of the dark house shows. The teaching concerns avoiding exposure that would bring a defect under scrutiny. Rav Tzadok uses it to explain why withholding a higher revelation can protect those whose earlier fault has not yet been fully repaired.

paragraphs.text: Shaar HaGilgulim, Introduction 22 — “After a righteous person departs this world, he is prepared to ascend through great degrees in the World to Come, but not all at once. Immediately after his passing, he is punished to cleanse his more serious transgressions, and then he is admitted to one higher precinct. When his time comes to ascend to a still higher precinct, he is again punished to cleanse sins lighter than the first, and then he rises to a second, higher degree. Afterward he is again punished over fine points of the commandments, as slight as a hair, in the mystery of 'Around Him it is exceedingly stormy'; then they raise him to the true precinct appropriate to him.” The source describes successively finer purification as the soul advances. Rav Tzadok applies this pattern to the renewed scrutiny that accompanies Israel's elevation after its earlier forgiveness.

p: And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
could be an atonement for the soul,
that he said, "All that a man has
he will give for his life,"
is more precious than all wealth,
so how is it possible to give money
as an atonement for the soul?
And the Holy One, blessed is He, showed him
from beneath the Throne of Glory
and said to him, "This they shall give —
The intent is that He showed him
that even though it is a piece of inanimate matter,
For in everything there is spirituality,
from which comes its coming into being and its existence,
for were it not so, it would have no existence,
since it is written, "There is none else besides Him"
And in all of a person's possessions
that belongs to the person's soul,
as is known: "and You give life to them all"
And this is the meaning of "they emptied out Egypt":
"so that that righteous man should not say..." etc.,
"'with great wealth' He did not fulfill"
But if Hashem, may He be blessed, wanted
what need was there to carry it from Egypt?
"Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold,
And also Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai,
as they said in the Yerushalmi
(בְּרָכוֹת פֶּרֶק ט הֲלָכָה ב סה, א)
with golden dinars," and it was filled.
And even without this, Avraham Avinu,
peace be upon him, did not ask for his offspring
and would not complain about this.
But the essence of "they emptied out" is known:
that they made it like the deep
meaning that there remained in them
for the beginning of the creation of living things
And according to the one who says, "like a trap
this is something that sustains life
and gives understanding to a person,
that a child does not know
until he tastes the taste of grain.
that one then distances oneself from his excrement;
of all the wisdom of Egypt,
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א, נה
And about this they said (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:55,
and so it is in the Mechilta, Bo 13,
that the plunder at the Sea was greater
This means that at the Exodus from Egypt
they were in the full force of love
for Hashem, may He be blessed,
corresponds to Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him.
For Egypt is "the nakedness of the land,"
and "whose issue is like the issue of horses,"
and this is the root of their vitality
and all their knowledge and wisdom
and their thoughts and the sustaining of their life;
and this is through holy sparks
that fell in the shattering of the vessels,
and through this there was aroused in them
the full force of holy love;
and this is "the point of silver,"
כִּי דָּבָר זֶה הָיָה רַק לְשָׁעָה
because this was only for a time,
and afterward it departed, as is known,
And at the splitting of the Yam Suf it says,
the attribute of fear is called gold,
And even though love is greater,
that is from the standpoint of the level itself,
for certainly the attribute of love
but from the standpoint of a person's own effort,
"Everything is in the hands of Heaven
and "the Holy One, blessed is He, has nothing..." etc.,
"but a treasury of the fear of Heaven";
of its own accord, as is known
from the principle "it is the way of a man..." etc.
And the fact that Egypt was a place of sorcery,
so that no slave could escape from there —
זֶה הָיָה עַל יְדֵי נִיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת
from the attribute of Gevurah of the shattering.
And sorcery is nullified by water,
that is, because their power is from Gevurah and fire,
and water, which is chassadim, extinguishes fire.
And therefore they were drowned in the water,
And this was through the plunder,
which was, in its plain sense, wealth,
as stated explicitly in the verse (Shemos 12:35) regarding Egypt.
And it is in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory,
and so it is in Yalkut Shimoni
in the name of Tanchuma (Yashan, Beshalach 16))
And this is because in the wealth
And likewise, the opposite also exists,
such as Yaakov's gift to Esav,
which is in the manner of
as they said in the Zohar
when he touched the hollow of his thigh,
that there was still a claim against him
because of the mixture of good and evil
in the sin of Adam HaRishon —
"for there is no righteous man..." etc. —
and that in him too there is some aspect
"When the wicked one is found guilty,
he takes his own portion and his fellow's portion
for every soul has a counterpart
which is the counterpart of the Adam of holiness
And just as there are there
כֵּן בָּזֶה יֵשׁ אֵיזֶה נְקוּדָּה מִשָּׁם
so in this one there is some point from there,
and it is necessary to sift them,
so that this one takes all the good
and that one all the evil
And so were Yaakov and Esav,
who are the root of good and evil.
And after he sent Esav his portion,
and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shabbos 33b):
in his body, in his wealth and in his Torah;
for what was lost from his wealth,
on the contrary, brought about for him
when he separated off what was not good.
And through this he was also healed
And so too in his Torah,
for the touching of the hollow of his thigh
corresponds to the breaking of the Tablets,
which caused forgetting of the Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֵירוּבִין נד, א)
as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Eruvin 54a);
and the attribute of truth belongs to Yaakov,
for Yaakov corresponds to the stone Tablets
or the parchment sheets of the Sefer Torah,
on which the letters are written,
this is Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
who is the root of the entire Torah,
which is called by his name, "the Torah of Moshe,"
and is also called "the Torah of truth."
And he was made whole in everything
that it is counted as tzedakah;
and they said (ibid.): If he merits,
"Is it not to share your bread with the hungry..." etc.;
is so that through this they absorb
and if they merit, it is rectified
so that from the evil, good is made.
And this too is the atonement for the soul
which alludes to the ten sefiros,
as they said in the Raaya Mehemna,
at the beginning of Parshas Ki Sisa,
that it alludes to the completeness
and the letter yud alludes to Chochmah,
and it is also alluded to in Rashi
that the yud is on account of thought.
And it is the beginning of revelation,
and it is the soul in the brain,
Until here from his holy manuscript.

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Sisa 11 — “Rabbi Yehudah bar Ilai said: When Moshe heard it, he began reasoning within himself: We find that the ransom of a human life is a talent of silver; each person in Israel will therefore have to give a talent of silver. Rav Tzadok probes how material wealth can answer to the value of a soul and why a visible demonstration was required.

paragraphs.text: Shemos Rabbah 52:3 — “One of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai's disciples went abroad and returned wealthy. The other disciples saw him, envied him, and wished to leave as well. Rabbi Shimon knew, brought them out to a valley before Meron, prayed, and said: ‘Valley, valley, fill with golden dinars!’ It began to draw forth golden dinars before them. paragraphs.text: Bava Basra 9a — “Rabbi Elazar said: When the Beis HaMikdash stood, a person would weigh out his shekel and gain atonement. Now that the Beis HaMikdash does not stand, if they give charity, it is well; if not, the nations of the world come and take by force. Even so, it is reckoned for them as charity, as it is stated: ‘Your exactors—charity.’ ... If he merits: ‘Is it not to share your bread with the hungry?’ If he does not merit: ‘You will bring the wandering poor into your house.’” The two teachings contrast willing charity with money taken through external pressure. Rav Tzadok understands these as paths by which the evil element associated with a person’s wealth is removed or transformed.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Tanya, Likkutei Amarim, chapter 37, paragraphs 19–20 — “There is no commandment in which the vital soul is invested as fully as in the commandment of charity. In all the other commandments, only one power of the vital soul is invested, and only while the commandment is being performed. But when a person gives charity from the work of his hands, the whole strength of his vital soul has been invested in his labor or other occupation through which he earned this money. When he gives it to charity, his entire vital soul ascends to Hashem. Even someone who does not live from his own labor nevertheless gives the life of his soul to Hashem, since with this money he could have purchased what sustains his vital soul.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 187b, Raaya Mehemna, Ki Sisa — “The commandment is to give half a shekel by the sacred shekel. The half shekel is like half a hin: vav, situated between the two hehs. The weight-stone is yud; ‘twenty gerah is the shekel’ is Yud. ‘The rich shall not increase’—this is the middle column, which must not exceed ten. Thus it is said in Sefer Yetzirah: Ten sefirot of restraint, ten and not eleven. ‘The poor shall not decrease’—this is the tzaddik; he must not diminish from ten, as it says, ten and not nine. ‘From half a shekel’—which is yud.” The ten-unit value is read as the complete tenfold structure. Rav Tzadok consequently understands the half-shekel's redemption of the soul as involving the wholeness of its spiritual configuration.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 123b, Mishpatim — “I saw Rabbi Shimon in a dream and asked him: We have learned that yud is Chochmah; why is heh Binah? He said: ‘A river goes forth from Eden to water the garden.’ The river from Eden is Binah, and yud is concealed within it. Yud spreads this river in every direction, forming heh. It then brings forth the son, vav. Thus we learned: Heh was originally dalet; when the male joined her, she conceived a son and was called heh. Afterward she gave birth to vav and placed him before her to nourish him.” The passage explicitly affirms the identification of yud with Chochmah and explains the extension from yud to heh through Binah. Rav Tzadok associates the ten gerah of the half-shekel with this beginning of revealed wisdom.

paragraphs.text: Rashi on Shemos 15:1 — “Then, when he saw the miracle, it arose in his heart that he should sing a song. ... Here too, ‘he will sing’ means that his heart told him he should sing, and so he did: ‘They said, saying: I will sing to Hashem.’ ... This teaches us that the yud was said with reference to the thought.” Rashi explains the grammatical yud of yashir through the thought preceding the act of singing. Rav Tzadok draws on that formulation as an allusion connecting yud and Chochmah.
